## 🚦 Risk level: **Amber** You’re handling user accounts and personal data (email, name, etc.). Fake sign‑ups can mess with your database, spike your free tier limits, and irritate real users. We’ll add a quick safety net and learn how to keep your app clean. --- ### 1️⃣ Ask a few clarifying questions (If you’re okay, just reply “I'm good”, and I’ll dive straight in.) 1. **Do you want every new account to confirm their email before they can sign in?** 2. **Do you want to show a simple captcha (e.g., Google reCAPTCHA v2) on the sign‑up form?** 3. **Do you want to limit how many accounts a single IP address can create in an hour?** --- ### 2️⃣ One‑screen plan (short, actionable) ``` What we are building: add email verification, captcha, and IP rate‑limit to signup. Who uses it: public, anytime Risk level: Amber (logins, personal data) Day‑one features: 1. Users receive a confirmation email with a link that must be clicked to activate. 2. A captcha widget blocks obvious bot traffic. 3. Creation requests from the same IP are throttled to 5 per hour. Information it stores: email, password, verified flag, signup_ip (optional) Logins: yes (only verified accounts) Money: no payments yet Built with: Supabase Auth + Cloud Functions + Firebase Firestore (or equivalent) Steps: 1. Enable “Confirm email” in Supabase Auth. 2. Add a reCAPTCHA widget to the signup form. 3. Add an edge function that blocks rapid sign‑ups from the same IP. Safety: secrets in .env, policy that only verified users can log in, save points before each change. Not in version one: email‑template customization, advanced spam filter. ``` **Does this look right? Reply “yes” or tell me what to tweak.** --- ### 3️⃣ If you want to jump straight in, here’s what to do (one change at a time, with proof) #### Step 1 – Enable email confirmation 1. Go to **Supabase → Auth → Settings → Email**. 2. Turn on **“Enable email confirmation”**. 3. **Proof**: We'll test by signing up with a test email and confirming. > **Tip** – Supabase automatically sends a one‑time link; no coding needed. #### Step 2 – Add a captcha to the UI 1. Sign up for a free reCAPTCHA v2 key at https://www.google.com/recaptcha/admin. 2. In your frontend code, add the script: ```html ``` 3. On your signup form, insert: ```html
``` 4. When the form submits, read `grecaptcha.getResponse()` and send it to your backend. 5. In Supabase, verify the token with Google’s API before creating the user. **Proof** – Try signing up. The form should not allow submission unless the captcha is passed. #### Step 3 – Throttle sign‑ups per IP (edge function) 1. Create a new edge function (Supabase > Functions > New). 2. Use this code skeleton (replace `YOUR_SECRET` with your Supabase secret key): ```ts import { serve } from 'std/server'; import { createSupabaseEdgeClient } from '@supabase/supabase-edge-js'; serve(async (req, env) => { const ip = req.headers.get('CF-Connecting-IP') || req.headers.get('X-Real-IP') || 'unknown'; const supabase = createSupabaseEdgeClient(env.SUPABASE_URL, env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY); // Look up how many users signed up from this IP in the last hour const { data: signups } = await supabase .from('signups_ip') .select('*') .eq('ip', ip) .gt('created_at', new Date(Date.now() - 60*60*1000).toISOString()); if (signups!.length >= 5) { return new Response('Too many requests from this IP. Try again later.', { status: 429 }); } // Record this attempt await supabase.from('signups_ip').insert({ ip, created_at: new Date() }); // Continue to the usual supabase auth create_user logic // (you'll need to forward the request body to Supabase's auth endpoint) }); ``` 3. Hook this function into your signup flow (redirect after the form submits, or call it as a proxy). 4. **Proof** – Simulate 6 sign‑ups from the same IP in an hour, the 6th should block. --- ### 4️⃣ Save points & safety - **Create a Git commit or zip** now as “before spam‑mitigation”. If anything breaks, you can revert. - Keep your email‑verification secret keys in `.env` (or the Supabase secrets panel). - Don’t expose your reCAPTCHA secret in the frontend. --- ### 5️⃣ Quick sanity check 1. **Sign up with a real email** → receive verification → sign in → works. 2. **Sign up with the same email again** → you get a “duplicate” warning. 3. **Falsify the captcha** → form won’t submit. 4. **Rapid‑fire sign‑ups from the same IP** → 5 succeed, 6th returns 429. If all four pass, you've slashed the fake sign‑up flow! --- **Next step:** Tell me which of the three steps (or all) you want to implement first, or if you’d like me to walk through a specific part of the code. I’ll keep the changes small and verify after each one.
